source_read: PMC HTML (PMC9289789), full text read in my own browser tab (page text read in three parts, the second and third with javascript): Summary, Introduction, Research in context panel, Methods, Results (9 paragraphs), Table 1 (structure and global rows), Table 2, Discussion (9 paragraphs), data sharing, declaration of interests, acknowledgments; Figure 2 viewed on screen for its legend (which cause groups are drawn as lower-risk); appendices 1-2 not read. The article carries a correction notice (Lancet 2022;400:358), not read.

claims.overstatement: By omission: the headline 'about 2.3 million to 2.8 million deaths a year' reads as the current model estimate, but this source (cited by the claim) reports that GBD 2020 attributed 1.78 million deaths (95% UI 1.39-2.27) to alcohol in 2020, lower than both figures and with an interval that does not overlap the 2016 one (2.4-3.3).
claims.note: The sentence citing this source is accurate: with the GBD 2016 relative-risk curves and GBD 2020 DALY weights the global, age-standardised, both-sexes TMREL was 0.534 (0-1.00) drinks a day, against 0 (0-0.800) published for 2016 and 0.511 (0.400-0.700) with the 2020 curves. 'The same group updated its weights' is a fair summary: the paper names three changes (five curves re-fitted, 2020 DALY weights, TMREL by region, age, sex and year) and the 0.534 figure isolates the weights. Suggest adding the GBD 2020 death estimate (cited by Bryazka as unpublished work by the same group), which also supports the claim's point that differences between rounds are not a trend.

anchors.extracted: Global, age-standardised, both-sexes TMREL: GBD 2016 curves with GBD 2016 weights 0 (0-0.800); GBD 2016 curves with GBD 2020 DALY weights 0.534 (0-1.00), NDE 0.669 (0-1.40); GBD 2020 curves and weights 0.511 (0.400-0.700), NDE 1.72 (0.80-3.30) drinks of 10 g a day.

Three changes from GBD 2016: five relative-risk curves updated, GBD 2020 DALY rates as weights, TMREL estimated by region, age, sex and year; the first two give a global TMREL of 0.511 (0.400-0.700); new weights with the old curves give 0.534 (0-1.00).
Alcohol use accounted for 1.78 million deaths (95% UI 1.39-2.27) in 2020 and was the leading risk factor for death among males aged 15-49 (cited to unpublished GBD 2020 work by Bryazka).

claims.note: The statement does not cite this source; it qualifies. Bryazka does not analyse deaths from all causes: its curves are DALY-weighted averages of 22 outcome curves. Relevant to the claim's sentence on genetic studies: in the meta-analysis of Mendelian randomisation studies cited by Bryazka, most cardiovascular and diabetes studies were null, but only 5 of 24 tested a non-linear relation, so most could neither show nor exclude a lower risk at low intake. Relevant to the dispute: the GBD 2020 model itself finds a J-shaped weighted curve at ages 40 and older in every region.

anchors.extracted: Authors argue that all-cause mortality is a poor basis for minimum-risk levels: causal pathways and confounding differ by cause, it includes causes unrelated to alcohol, and its cause composition differs between populations.

Observational estimates subject to reverse causation, selection bias and residual confounding; in a cited meta-analysis of Mendelian randomisation studies, 67% of cardiovascular and 75% of diabetes studies found no association with alcohol, and only 5 of 24 examined a non-linear relation.
At ages 40 and older the burden-weighted curve was J-shaped in all regions: TMREL 0.114 (0-0.403) to 1.87 (0.500-3.30), NDE 0.193 (0-0.900) to 6.94 (3.40-8.30) drinks a day.

claims.overstatement: Minor: (1) 'at about half a standard drink a day for people aged 40 and older' fits ages 40-64 (global 0.527 men, 0.562 women) but the global figures at 65 and older are about two thirds of a drink (0.636, 0.656), and regional values at 40 and older run from 0.114 to 1.87; (2) 'the authors expect that including the last three would lower the amounts' is firmer than the source, which says inclusion would possibly reduce the TMREL and NDE. Advice risk: the non-drinker-equivalence figures for older ages (3.19 and 3.51 drinks, about 32-35 g, a day at 65 and older) and 'about half a standard drink a day' could be read as amounts carrying no extra risk; the claim's caveat (population average, not a risk-free amount) is there but only at the end.
claims.note: Every GBD 2020 number in the statement and magnitude matches: 22 curves (6 outcomes updated with 71 more studies, lower respiratory infection dropped, 5 re-fitted, 17 kept from GBD 2016); TMREL for all populations 0 (0-0) to 1.87 (0.500-3.30); ages 15-39 TMREL 0 to 0.603 (0.400-1.00), NDE 0.002 (0-0) to 1.75 (0.698-4.30); global 15-39 men 0.136 (0-0.400) and 0.249 (0-1.00), women 0.273 (0-0.500) and 0.546 (0-1.30); injuries 66.3% (65.1-67.5) and 47.9% (46.0-49.8) of alcohol-related DALYs at 15-39; 40-64 men 0.527 (0.400-1.00) and 1.69 (0.800-3.20), women 0.562 (0.400-0.800) and 1.82 (1.00-3.10); 65+ men 0.636 (0.500-1.00) and 3.19 (1.50-5.20), women 0.656 (0.500-1.00) and 3.51 (1.70-5.50); 40+ across regions TMREL 0.114 (0-0.403) to 1.87, NDE 0.193 (0-0.900) to 6.94 (3.40-8.30); Table 2 values; sex differences not significant; hypothetical alcohol use disorder and cardiomyopathy curves lowered the TMREL by 0.058, 0.092 and 0.146 drinks a day on average. Editors' arithmetic recomputed at 10 g a drink: 0.249 = 2.49 g (about 2.5), 0.546 = 5.46 g (about 5.5), 0.511 = 5.11 g (about 5.1): same. 'The move away from zero comes mostly from the weights' agrees with Table 2 and with the authors' statement that results were not sensitive to the five updated curves. The editors' reading that lowest points above zero come from IHD, ischaemic stroke and diabetes agrees with Figure 2, whose lower-risk (green) groups are 'ischaemic heart disease and stroke' and diabetes; the main text never says which of the 22 curves dip below 1, and the green stroke group appears to include intracerebral haemorrhage (not listed in any other group). Also excluded from the 2020 curves: alcoholic cardiomyopathy (no curve). Reference group: the relative-risk curves use non-drinkers, with study-level covariates for how each study defined its reference group and for sick-quitter adjustment; the claim's 'compared with not drinking' fits. Small internal inconsistency: the Discussion gives the lowest NDE at 15-39 as 0 (0-0), the Summary and Results as 0.002 (0-0). The Summary's Interpretation (strong evidence to support recommendations varying by age and location) goes beyond a model built on observational curves; the claim does not adopt it.

anchors.extracted: TMREL across all populations 0 (0-0) to 1.87 (0.500-3.30) drinks a day; ages 15-39: TMREL 0 to 0.603 (0.400-1.00), NDE 0.002 (0-0) to 1.75 (0.698-4.30); injuries 66.3% (65.1-67.5) of alcohol-related DALYs in males and 47.9% (46.0-49.8) in females at 15-39; TMREL 0.136 (0-0.400) men and 0.273 (0-0.500) women, NDE 0.249 (0-1.00) and 0.546 (0-1.30); no significant sex or year differences.

Global TMREL at 40-64: 0.527 (0.400-1.00) men, 0.562 (0.400-0.800) women; NDE 1.69 (0.800-3.20) and 1.82 (1.00-3.10). At 65 and older: TMREL 0.636 (0.500-1.00) and 0.656 (0.500-1.00); NDE 3.19 (1.50-5.20) and 3.51 (1.70-5.50); IHD 31.5% and 29.7%, ischaemic stroke 14.2% and 16.0% of alcohol-related DALYs; sex differences not significant.

Global, age-standardised, both sexes: 2016 published TMREL 0 (0-0.800); 2016 curves with 2020 DALY weights 0.534 (0-1.00), NDE 0.669 (0-1.40); 2020 curves and weights 0.511 (0.400-0.700), NDE 1.72 (0.80-3.30); results not sensitive to the five updated curves.

anchors.locator: Methods > Estimating dose-response relative risks, 1st to 3rd paragraphs; Research in context > Added value of this study
anchors.extracted: GBD 2016 review: 592 cohort and case-control studies, 23 outcomes (listed). GBD 2020 updated six outcomes with 71 additional studies, dropped lower respiratory infection, re-fitted five curves with MR-BRT and kept 17 from GBD 2016 (22 curves); reference group non-drinkers, with bias covariates including reference-group definition and sick-quitter adjustment.

anchors.locator: Methods > Estimating TMREL and NDE, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Results, 8th paragraph
anchors.extracted: Weighted curves for each region, age, sex and year, weights = each cause's share of DALY rates; 22 of 24 outcomes, no curves for alcohol use disorder or alcoholic cardiomyopathy; hypothetical curves for these two lowered the TMREL on average by 0.058 (0.00-0.30), 0.092 (0.00-0.50) and 0.146 (0.00-0.60) drinks a day in three scenarios.

Estimates minimise health loss for a population; individual-level risk depends on comorbidity, medicines and other individual factors and is outside the study's scope; results for older adults carry additional uncertainty.

Limitations: drinking patterns (heavy episodic drinking) not incorporated; alcohol use disorders not in the TMREL calculation; possible residual bias (measurement, selection, reverse causality); relative risks rest on self-reported drinking; beverage type not considered; weights include alcohol-caused DALYs; major depressive disorder, generalised anxiety disorder and dementia not included, whose inclusion would possibly reduce TMREL and NDE.
Cited meta-analysis of Mendelian randomisation studies: 67% of cardiovascular and 75% of diabetes studies null; only 5 of 24 examined a non-linear relation.

Green shades mark causes with lower risk at low consumption than at none: the key's green groups are ischaemic heart disease and stroke, and diabetes; the other groups (cancers, cirrhosis, infectious disease, injuries, other causes) are drawn as harmful at all levels.

key_findings.correction: The count of 17 carried-over curves is stated in Research in context > Added value of this study; the Methods give 22 curves with 5 re-fitted.
Minor: the source gives the 0 to 1.87 range across geography, age, sex and time, not for 2020 only; the 2020 values by age group have the same extremes, so no number changes.
The note is borne out by the Figure 2 legend, which says the proportions are the weights of the cause-specific curves.

Recomputed from Table 1's global rows: males 595 + 363 + 69.9 = 1028 million (1.03 billion), females 195 + 98.6 + 18.4 = 312 million, total 1.34 billion, male share 76.7% against the printed 76.9% (rounding).
Recomputed: men 15-39 595 of 790 million aged 15-39 above the NDE = 75.3% (printed 75.5%); aged 65 and older 88.3 of 1340 million = 6.6% (printed 6.55%); 14 + 55 + 135 = 204 countries.
Reference 6 is van de Luitgaarden et al., Eur J Epidemiol 2021.
The source says inclusion of depression, anxiety and dementia would possibly (not probably) reduce the TMREL and NDE. The rest is confirmed.
Checked on PMC (PMC9350421): appendices 1 and 2 corrected as of 19 July 2022; no change to the main text is described.

reporting_issues.note: Table 1 global rows checked: significant decreases for males 15-39 (-4.62%, -6.27 to -2.64), females 40-64 (-4.22%, -6.54 to -0.279) and females 65+ (-1.96%, -3.63 to -0.448); non-significant for the other three groups; Results, 6th paragraph speaks first of drinkers, then of the population.
14 + 55 + 135 = 204, the number of countries and territories; period given as 1990-2019 against a table headed 2020.
Found independently in my blind reading.
Griswold 2018, Methods > Systematic review and meta-analysis, 2nd paragraph, describes mixed-effects logistic regression with non-linear splines.

Results, 8th paragraph: not sensitive to the approach to constructing the weighted curves (scenarios in the appendix); Results, 9th paragraph: not sensitive to the five updated curves; neither explains the move from 0 to 0.534 with the weights alone.

risk_of_bias.note: Overall high agrees: the TMRELs above zero depend wholly on the protective dips of observational curves and on the weights, and the 2016-to-2020 shift with unchanged curves shows the weight dependence. Domain judgments agree.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. Items checked against the text: sex point estimates higher for women in every age group (TMREL and NDE at 15-39, 40-64 and 65+); 'harmful' defined as above the mean NDE (Figure 4 legend); lowest regional TMREL at 40+ 0.114 with an interval from 0.

missed: Introduction, 1st paragraph: GBD 2020 attributed 1.78 million deaths (95% UI 1.39-2.27) to alcohol in 2020 (cited as unpublished work); not a key finding on this card, though it appears in the Griswold card's 'where it stands' and bears directly on cl_alc_deaths_global, whose 2.3-2.8 million range omits it.

Figure 2 key: the green (lower risk at low intake) groups are 'ischaemic heart disease and stroke' and diabetes; intracerebral haemorrhage is not listed in any other group, so it appears to sit in the green stroke group, and the main text never says which of the 22 curves dip below 1. Worth recording beside the card's statement that the dips for ischaemic heart disease, ischaemic stroke and diabetes create every non-zero TMREL.

Discussion, 4th paragraph: the authors place individual-level risk outside the study's scope and say results for older adults carry additional uncertainty; the card uses this in cannot_establish but has no key finding with its locator, which claims citing the population-not-person reading would need.
